3.name: Primal Companion
3.notes:
You magically summon a primal beast—Beast of the Land, Sea, or Sky. You determine its appearance, and it bears supernatural primal markings. The beast is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands.

Combat. The beast takes its turn on yours. It can move and take Reactions independently, but only takes the Dodge action unless you use a Bonus Action to command it to take an action in its stat block or another action. You may also sacrifice one of your attacks from the Attack action to command it to use its Beast's Strike action. If you are Incapacitated, it acts on its own and is not restricted to Dodge.

Restoring or Replacing the Beast. If the beast died within the last hour, you may use a Magic action to touch it and expend a spell slot, returning it to life after 1 minute with full Hit Points. After each Long Rest, you can summon a different primal beast; the previous one vanishes when the new one appears.

7.name: Exceptional Training
7.notes:
When you take a Bonus Action to command your Primal Companion to take an action, you can also command it to take Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help using its Bonus Action.

Additionally, whenever the beast hits with an attack and deals damage, it can deal Force damage instead of its normal damage type.

11.name: Bestial Fury
11.notes:
When you command your Primal Companion to use its Beast's Strike action, it can use it twice.

The first time each turn it hits a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark spell, it deals extra Force damage equal to the spell's bonus damage.

15.name: Share Spells
15.notes: When you cast a spell that targets only yourself, you may also affect your Primal Companion with the spell if it is within 30 feet of you.
